neighbours.label: a parenthetical interjection set off by commas inside a sentence ('you know', 'we found', 'she said'); the same words used as the main verb of a sentence stay quiet
fire: The old harbor town, you know, used to be full of fishing boats.
Mice that slept less, we found, made more mistakes in the maze.
The new bakery on the corner, she said, sells the best bread in town.
My cousin, you know, never learned to ride a bicycle.
Students who read aloud, we found, remembered more of the story.
The road to the lake, he said, is closed until the spring.
That summer was, you know, the hottest one I can remember.
Plants grown near the window, they found, flowered two weeks earlier.
quiet: The old harbor town used to be full of fishing boats every summer.
Mice that slept less made more mistakes in the maze than the others.
The new bakery on the corner sells the best bread in town.
My cousin never learned to ride a bicycle as a child.
Students who read aloud remembered more of the story than the rest.
The road to the lake is closed until the spring thaw.
That summer was the hottest one I can remember in this valley.
Plants grown near the window flowered two weeks earlier than the rest.

predictions: fire 0.25-0.45 on the interjection; near misses below 0.1
notes: Card: know x4, she/said, found, opening quote, '#'. Probe: ', we found,' 0.424, ', you know,' 0.402, ', she said,' 0.381, quote before speech 0.242; 'You know the answer' 0.036, 'We found a wallet' 0.015, same sentence without the interjection 0.054. Caveat: ', and that was why' scored 0.356, so the pole is not specific to interjections; near misses avoid comma + 'and that'.
